cases.query: Is classical Ashwagandha churna as per Charaka Samhita patentable in India?
contexts: An invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component(s) — is not patentable. Sec 3(p) Patents Act
cases.answer: No. Under Sec 3(p) Patents Act, a formulation verbatim from a classical text is traditional knowledge and not patentable. TKDL may be cited as prior art. [Patents Act, 1970 — Sec 3(p)]

cases.query: I made a novel Ashwagandha extract with 10x withanolide by new process — can I patent it?
contexts: Proprietary with novel process/dosage is patentable if novelty+inventive step satisfied
Biological resource access requires NBA/SBB benefit-sharing
cases.answer: Yes, if novel and inventive. File patent + disclose TK origin under WIPO GRATK Art 3 and comply with BDA Sec 7 ABS via SBB/NBA.

cases.query: WIPO GRATK disclosure requirement for PCT filing with Indian genetic resource
contexts: Where the claimed invention is based on genetic resources, each Contracting Party shall require applicants to disclose the country of origin — Art 3.1 WIPO GRATK 2024
cases.answer: Under Art 3 GRATK 2024, disclose country of origin/source of genetic resource and associated TK. Attach PIC/MAT from NBA.

cases.query: Do I need NBA approval to export aloe vera sourced in Kerala for cosmetic manufacture?
contexts: Access to biological resources for commercial utilization requires prior intimation to SBB / approval of NBA
cases.answer: Yes — ABS applies. Indian entity: intimate SBB before commercial access; if foreign buyer, NBA approval + benefit-sharing under BDA Sec 7/21.

cases.query: Can I sell chyawanprash as food under FSSAI Ayurveda Aahar or as drug?
contexts: Ayurveda Aahar means food recipes described in authoritative Ayurveda texts, with claim restrictions
cases.answer: If recipe is in authoritative text and consumed as food → FSSAI Aahar (Reg 3(1), 2022). If therapeutic dosage/claim → AYUSH drug license. Magic Remedies Act bars cure-all claims.
